question: Should OpenClaw core own a first-class signed publisher-follow lifecycle and `openclaw publisher` CLI now, or should this remain outside core until the RFC and marketplace ownership model are approved?
rationale: The branch creates a permanent core protocol, trust, storage, and CLI surface tied to an emerging ClawHub producer contract; tests cannot decide whether that ownership and rollout sequence match maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve staged core landing
options.body: Approve the core direction, land the verifier, transport, and state prerequisites separately, then review a rebased follow-lifecycle slice.

options.title: Keep the stack paused
options.body: Leave the draft stack open until the RFC, producer contract, and user-facing lifecycle are explicitly approved together.

options.title: Move lifecycle outside core
options.body: Keep generic verification seams in core if needed, but implement publisher following through a plugin or ClawHub-owned package.

recommendation.title: Approve staged core landing
recommendation.body: Approve the core direction, land the verifier, transport, and state prerequisites separately, then review a rebased follow-lifecycle slice.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision concerns permanent core scope, marketplace ownership, and user-facing product direction rather than a mechanical implementation detail.
